legend: R = read or fetched during this project. M = tool used here; the citation details were written from memory and should be checked before the proposal is submitted. S = found in a web search, source document not identified. N = taken from the team's notes, not read.
refs: NCBI Sequence Read Archive / BioProject: PRJNA1433044 (Universitas Padjadjaran, Bandung active case finding; the design set), also PRJNA595834, PRJNA430531, PRJNA1150781, PRJNA633244, PRJNA950554. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/
SRA public metadata, AWS Open Data, s3://sra-pub-metadata-us-east-1/sra/metadata/ (queried with DuckDB); ENA file reports for read sizes, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/
H37Rv reference genome, NCBI RefSeq NC_000962.3. Cole ST et al. Deciphering the biology of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from the complete genome sequence. Nature 393:537-544 (1998).
Gene annotation: Ensembl Genomes, assembly ASM19595v2 (GCA_000195955.2), file taken from the TOAST repository (MIT licence).

World Health Organization. Catalogue of mutations in Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex and their association with drug resistance, 2nd edition (2023). Data files: https://github.com/GTB-tbsequencing/mutation-catalogue-2023 (MIT licence).

Low-confidence region mask: Marin M et al. Benchmarking the empirical accuracy of short-read sequencing across the M. tuberculosis genome. Bioinformatics 38(7):1781-1787 (2022); file from https://github.com/nextstrain/tb (defaults/AF14_RLC_Regions.Plus.LowPmapK50E4.H37Rv.bed).

Off-target genomes via NCBI Datasets, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/ : human GRCh38 (GCF_000001405.40) and reference genomes of seven non-tuberculous mycobacteria and six respiratory bacteria (list in the handover).
Seemann T. snippy: rapid haploid variant calling and core genome alignment, v4.6.0. https://github.com/tseemann/snippy
Garrison E, Marth G. Haplotype-based variant detection from short-read sequencing. arXiv:1207.3907 (2012) (FreeBayes 1.3.6, run inside snippy).
Li H. Aligning sequence reads, clone sequences and assembly contigs with BWA-MEM. arXiv:1303.3997 (2013).
Phelan JE et al. Integrating informatics tools and portable sequencing technology for rapid detection of resistance to anti-tuberculous drugs. Genome Medicine 11:41 (2019) (TB-Profiler 6.6.5).
Hall M. Rasusa: randomly subsample sequencing reads to a specified coverage. Journal of Open Source Software 7(69):3941 (2022) (v5.1.0).
Mölder F et al. Sustainable data analysis with Snakemake. F1000Research 10:33 (2021).
Raasveldt M, Mühleisen H. DuckDB: an embeddable analytical database. SIGMOD 2019.
Untergasser A et al. Primer3: new capabilities and interfaces. Nucleic Acids Research 40(15):e115 (2012); Python bindings primer3-py 2.4.0, https://github.com/libnano/primer3-py
Camacho C et al. BLAST+: architecture and applications. BMC Bioinformatics 10:421 (2009) (blastn 2.17.0+).

Ye J et al. Primer-BLAST: a tool to design target-specific primers for polymerase chain reaction. BMC Bioinformatics 13:134 (2012). The off-target product screen is inspired by it but is not identical to its defaults.

Google Cloud Vertex AI and Gemini (model gemini-3.5-flash-lite, location global), https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai ; google-genai SDK; FastAPI, https://fastapi.tiangolo.com ; Next.js 16, https://nextjs.org/docs (bundled docs read) ; Tailwind CSS 4.

Wang L et al. TOAST: a novel tool for designing targeted gene amplicons and an optimised set of primers for high-throughput sequencing in tuberculosis genomic studies. BMC Genomics 26:1058 (2025). doi:10.1186/s12864-025-12247-9 ; https://github.com/linfeng-wang/TOAST

Wang Y et al. Accelerating primer design for amplicon sequencing using large language model-powered agents (PrimeGen). Nature Biomedical Engineering 10:338-353 (2026). doi:10.1038/s41551-025-01455-z ; https://github.com/melobio/PrimeGen

Nextstrain TB build, https://nextstrain.org/tb/global and https://github.com/nextstrain/tb : the per-isolate processing (SRA metadata query, fasterq-dump, TB-Profiler, snippy, Snakemake) is modelled on it.

Xie NG et al. Designing highly multiplex PCR primer sets with Simulated Annealing Design using Dimer Likelihood Estimation (SADDLE). Nature Communications 13:1881 (2022). Cited in the PrimeGen paper; not used in the code.

Multiplex real-time PCR melting curve assay to detect drug-resistant mutations of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Journal of Clinical Microbiology (2011). https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21752982 : found in a web search; the basis for the melt-probe idea for dense regions such as the rpoB RRDR.

Comparative genomic analysis of established and emerging anti-tubercular drug targets ... in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Indonesia. Frontiers in Tropical Diseases (2026). doi:10.3389/fitd.2026.1953716 : listed in the team notes (master document p. 76); not read.
GenoHack Master Document (team notes, Indonesian), including the meeting plan 'Kesimpulan Meet 23/10/26' (p. 81) and the draft proposal with its own reference list (pp. 68-72).

Design thresholds: the TOAST default settings file and the PrimeGen paper (both read); a web search result (patent text, specific patent not identified) for probe Tm 8-12 C above the primers and amplicons of 50-150 bp; general qPCR practice from memory. The dimer limit of about -9 kcal/mol is the commonly quoted manufacturer guidance, not verified here. See handover section 9.
